newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Apple Fields to make statement on future.
newsitem.headline: Apple Fields to make statement on future.

text.p: Orchardist Apple Fields Ltd said it would hold a news conference on Wednesday to announce its future plans after what it called the "stunning" refusal of its export application licence by the Apple and Pear Marketing Board.
The board, which controls apple and pear exports, declined the application on the grounds it would damage the rest of the industry.

Apple Fields said in mid-November it would bulldoze all of its trees and quit the pipfruit business unless it was granted an export licence for a proposed joint venture with four leading fruit distributors in the United States, Europe and Asia.
It wanted a licence to export its total crop, around 1.5 million cartons.
If the licence was refused, Apple Fields said it would move into the property development business.
The company said it was now locked in discussions with its lawyers and international partners.
Managing Director Tom Kain said the board's decision was a tragedy for the New Zealand apple industry, which would now inevitably continue to decline.
